extracted.intended_audience: Postdoctoral researchers and prospective applicants for NLM/NIH K99/R00 career development awards
extracted.subtask_description: Official FAQ guidance for preparing and determining eligibility for the NLM-specific K99/R00 (NIH career development) application and activation of the R00 phase. Covers eligibility, effort, allowable costs, review, and pre-submission consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution change for R00 phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Although it's not a requirement for a K99 awardee to change institutions for the R00 phase, the awardee is encouraged to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most of NLM's K99 awardees do change institutions for their R00 phases. Changing institutions is encouraged but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty position not required at time of application
rubrics_metrics.description: No, you don't have to have a faculty position when you apply for a K99.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial 1-2 year K99 phase is a mentored phase and doesn't require a faculty position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation of R00 for intramural postdocs / eligible extramural appointment required
rubrics_metrics.description: You'll have to secure an independent research position, preferably a tenure-track assistant professor position (or equivalent) at an eligible extramural institution, to activate the R00 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may apply for an independent phase position within the NIH intramural research program (IRP), but if you accept an IRP position the independent phase of the award will not be activated because NIH intramural scientists are supported by NIH intramural funds and are not eligible for NIH extramural grant awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-year postdoctoral training limit counted at application
rubrics_metrics.description: "no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research training at the time of application"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 4-year postdoc training limit is counted as of the day the application is submitted (not the award date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Which study section reviews NLM K99/R00 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All K99 applications assigned to NLM are reviewed by an NLM study section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLM's study section is the Biomedical Library and Informatics Review Committee (BLIRC); the Scientific Review Officer may add ad hoc reviewers if additional expertise is needed. BLIRC membership is listed at the provided roster link.

rubrics_metrics.name: NLM funding commitment and award decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: NLM does not have a set commitment for each of its grant programs; general funding guidelines are established each year based on appropriated funds available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final award decisions reflect considerations of program relevance, portfolio balance, recommendations of the NLM Board of Regents, and availability of funds. Historically, NLM has funded about 3 new K99/R00 awards per year on average.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 awardees considered 'new investigators' for R01
rubrics_metrics.description: K99/R00 awardees remain eligible to be considered 'new investigators' when applying for their first NIH R01 support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum research effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of this award must devote a minimum of 75 percent effort to the proposed research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remaining 25 percent effort can be divided among other clinical and teaching activities only if consistent with career development into a research informatician. Under unusual and pressing circumstances an awardee may request a reduction below 75% (considered case-by-case), but in no case will effort below 50% be permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of K99 start-up funds and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to $20,000 per year will be provided to cover expenses of starting up a research program, including tuition/fees related to career development, salaries for technical support, consultant costs, equipment, supplies, travel to meetings/training, statistical services, and other research-related expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions: Salary for mentors, secretarial and administrative assistance, etc., is NOT allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational eligibility to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Only domestic nonprofit, public or private institutions, such as medical, dental or nursing schools or other institutions of higher education may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants working for for-profit dot.com companies are not eligible to apply as the applicant organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor / co-mentor structure
rubrics_metrics.description: You can have co-mentors if your career development plan and/or project require mentors with complementary expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should usually have one primary mentor and then one or more co-mentors as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting T15 fellowship years toward postdoc limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether years in a T15 program count depends on whether you were a predoctoral or a postdoctoral fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Years as a predoctoral fellow do not count toward the 4-year postdoctoral research training limit; years as a postdoctoral fellow do count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application program officer feedback (limited scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can send a program officer a one-page description/Specific Aims page for feedback before applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program officer will tell you if the idea is in scope for the program or needs further work, but this will not be an in-depth evaluation of scientific merit—the scientific review is done by the study section.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 mentored phase typical duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial K99 phase is a mentored phase lasting 1-2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates the expected duration of mentored support prior to the independent R00 phase.
